questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: What is dimensions of energy in terms of linear momentum (P), area (A) and Time (T)
questions.solution:
Dimensions of energy in terms of momentum (P). Area (A) and Time (T), is related of
$\mathrm{E}=\mathrm{P}^{\mathrm{a}} \mathrm{A}^{\mathrm{b}} \mathrm{T}^{\mathrm{C}}\ldots(i)$
Writing dimensional formula of both side,
$\begin{aligned}
& {\left[\mathrm{ML}^2 \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\right]=\left[\mathrm{MLT}^{-1}\right]^a\left[L^2\right]^b[\mathrm{~T}]^{\mathrm{c}}} \\

&
\end{aligned}$
Comparing the exponents, $\mathrm{a}=1, \mathrm{a}+2 \mathrm{~b}=2\begin{gathered}
2 \mathrm{~b}=1 \\
\mathrm{~b}=\frac{1}{2} \\
-\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{c}=-2-1+\mathrm{c}=-2 \\
\Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{C}=-1
\end{gathered}\therefore$ Form Eq. (i), we have
$\Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{E}=\left[\mathrm{PA}^{1 / 2} \mathrm{~T}^{-1}\right]$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Find the average velocity when a particle complete the circle of radius 1 m in 10 sec .
questions.solution:
When particle completes one revolution in circular motion, then average displacement travelled by particle is zero.
Hence, Average velocity
$=\frac{\text { average displacement }}{\Delta \mathrm{t}}=\frac{0}{\Delta \mathrm{t}}=0$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Speeds of a particle at 3rd and 8th sec are $20 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ and zero respectively, then average acceleration between 3 rd and 8th sec will be
questions.solution:
Time interval between 8 th sec. and 3rd sec $\Delta \mathrm{t}=8-3=5 \mathrm{~s}$
i.e. $\Delta t=5 \mathrm{~s}$
Change in velocity $\Delta \mathrm{V}=20-0=20 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\therefore$ Average acceleration $=\frac{\Delta \mathrm{V}}{\Delta \mathrm{t}}=\frac{20}{5}=4 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle is projected at an angle of $30^{\circ}$ from the horizontal with a speed of $10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ on the earth. It's time of flight, range, velocity of impact are respectively $\mathrm{T}, \mathrm{R}, \mathrm{V}$. If this projectile is projected on the moon then its time of flight, range and velocity of impact is (assume gravitational field on moon is $\mathrm{g} / 6 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ )
questions.solution:
Given, angle of projection, $\theta=30^{\circ}$ Initial speed of particle, $\mathrm{v}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
Time of flights, range and velocity of impact on the surface of earth are T, R and V respectively
$\therefore \quad \mathrm{T}=\frac{2 \mathrm{v} \sin \theta}{\mathrm{g}}, \mathrm{R}=\frac{\mathrm{v}^2 \sin 2 \theta}{\mathrm{g}}$
Gravitational acceleration on moon's surface is equal to $\frac{1}{6}$ part of gravitational acceleration on the earth's surface.
Hence,
$\begin{aligned}
& g_m=\frac{g_e}{6} \\
& T_m=\frac{2 v \sin \theta}{\frac{g}{6}}=\frac{6 \times 2 v \sin \theta}{g}=6 \mathrm{~T} \\
& R_m=\frac{v^2 \sin 2 \theta}{\frac{g}{6}}=\frac{6 v^2 \sin 2 \theta}{g}=6 R
\end{aligned}$
Velocity of impact will be same at both places of moon and earth.
$\therefore \quad \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{m}}=\mathrm{V}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The rate of decrease of kinetic energy is 9.6 J/s. Find the magnitude of force acting on particle when it's speed is $3 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$.
questions.solution:
Given, rate of decrease in kinetic energy
$\frac{\mathrm{dk}}{\mathrm{dt}}=9.6 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{s}$
When, speed, $\mathrm{v}=3 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ then force $\mathrm{F}=$ ?
Kinetic energy $\mathrm{k}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}^2$
differentiating with respect to ' $t$ ', we have
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{\mathrm{dk}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~m} \cdot 2 \mathrm{v} \frac{\mathrm{dv}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\mathrm{v} \cdot \mathrm{m} \frac{\mathrm{dv}}{\mathrm{dt}} \\
& =v . m \frac{\mathrm{dp}}{\mathrm{dt}} \\
& \frac{\mathrm{dk}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\mathrm{v} . \mathrm{F} \quad\left[\because \text { force } \mathrm{F}=\frac{\mathrm{mdp}}{\mathrm{dt}}\right]
\therefore \quad \mathrm{F}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{v}} \cdot \frac{\mathrm{dk}}{\mathrm{dt}}
\\ & =\frac{1}{3} \times 9.6=3.2 \mathrm{~N} \\ &\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A particle of mass 7 kg is executing circular motion with time period of 11 sec . Find out centripetal force, if radius of circle is 10 m .

questions.q: If a ball of mass 0.1 kg hits the ground from the height of 20 m and bounce back to the same height, then find out the force exerted on the ball if the time of impact is 0.04 sec . (Take, $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ )
questions.solution:
Here, mass of ball $m=0.1 \mathrm{~kg}$
Velocity attained by the ball before hitting the
$\begin{aligned}
\text { ground }(\mathrm{v}) & =\sqrt{2 \mathrm{gh}}(-\hat{\mathrm{j}}) \\
& =\sqrt{2 \times 10 \times 20}(-\hat{\mathrm{j}})=-20 \hat{\mathrm{j}} / \mathrm{s}
\end{aligned}$
Velocity of ball when bounce back to the same height after hitting the ground,
$V^{\prime}=-v=-(-20 \hat{j})=20 \hat{j} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\therefore$ Change in velocity
$\Delta V=V^{\prime}-V=20 \hat{j}-(-20 \hat{j})=40 \hat{j} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\therefore$ Force exerted on the ball
$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{f} & =\frac{\Delta \mathrm{P}}{\Delta \mathrm{t}}=\frac{\mathrm{m} \Delta \mathrm{V}}{0.04}[\text { given } \Delta \mathrm{t}=0.04] \\
& =\frac{0.1 \times 40 \hat{\mathrm{j}}}{0.04}=100 \mathrm{~N}(\hat{\mathrm{j}})
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.q: A toy truck of mass 2 m elastically collides with a toy car of mass $m$. speed of truck is $v$ and car is at rest. Find the velocity of car after collision.
questions.solution:
Mass of toy truck $m_t=2 \mathrm{~m}$
Mass of toy car $\mathrm{m}_c=\mathrm{m}$
Initial speed of truck $v_t=v$
and initial speed of car $u_c=0$
If $v_1$ and $v_2$ be the final velocity of truck and car after collision, then by law of conservation of momentum,
Total initial momentum $=$ total final momentum
$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{t}} \cdot \mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{t}}+\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{c}} \mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{c}} & =\mathrm{m}_4 \mathrm{v}_1+\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{c}} \mathrm{v}_2 \\
2 \mathrm{mv}+0 & =2 \mathrm{mv}_1+\mathrm{mv}_2 \\
2 \mathrm{v} & =2 \mathrm{v}_1+\mathrm{v}_2
\end{aligned}$
For elastic collision, coefficient of restitution, $e=1$
i.e.
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{v_2-v_1}{u_1-u_c}=1 \\
& \frac{v_2-v_1}{v-0}=1 \Rightarrow v=v_2-v_1
\end{aligned}$
Solving Eqs. (i) and (ii), we have $\mathrm{v}_2=\frac{4 \mathrm{v}}{3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two disc having mass ratio $1 / 2$ and diameter ratio $2 / 1$ then find ratio of moment of inertia.
questions.solution:
Given, mass ratio of two disc
$\mathrm{m}_1: \mathrm{m}_2=1: 2 \text { i.e. } \frac{\mathrm{m}_1}{\mathrm{~m}_2}=\frac{1}{2}$
and diameter ratio $\frac{\mathrm{d}_1}{\mathrm{~d}_2}=\frac{2}{1} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{r}_1}{\mathrm{r}_2}=\frac{2}{1}\therefore$ Ratio of their moment of inertia,
$\begin{array}{ll}
\quad \frac{\mathrm{I}_1}{\mathrm{I}_2}= & \frac{\frac{\mathrm{m}_1 \mathrm{r}_1^2}{2}}{\frac{\mathrm{m}_2 \mathrm{r}_2^2}{2}}=\frac{\mathrm{m}_1}{\mathrm{~m}_2} \cdot\left(\frac{\mathrm{r}_1}{\mathrm{r}_2}\right)^2=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{2}{1}\right)^2=\frac{2}{1} \\
\therefore \quad \mathrm{I}_1: \mathrm{I}_2=2: 1
\end{array}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If escape velocity on earth surface is $11.1 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$, then find the escape velocity on moon surface. If mass of moon is $\frac{1}{81}$ times of mass of earth and radius of moon is $\frac{1}{4}$ times radius of earth.
questions.solution:
Given, Escape velocity on the surface of earth, $\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{e}}=11.1 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$
i.e.
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{e}}=\sqrt{2 \mathrm{gR}_{\mathrm{e}}} \\
& \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{e}}=\sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{GM}_{\mathrm{e}}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}}}
\end{aligned}$
Mass of moon, $M_m=\frac{M_e}{81}$
Radius of moon, $\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{m}}=\frac{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{e}}}{4}\therefore$ Escape velocity on the surface of moon
$\begin{aligned}
& v_m=\sqrt{\frac{2 G M_m}{R_m}}=\sqrt{\frac{2 G \frac{M e}{81}}{\frac{R_e}{4}}} \\
& =\frac{2 \sqrt{2}}{9} \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{GM}_{\mathrm{c}}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{c}}}}=\frac{2}{9} \sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{GM}_{\mathrm{c}}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{c}}}}=\frac{2}{9} \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{e}}=\frac{2}{9} \times 11.1=2.46 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h} \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two wire of same material having radius in ratio $2: 1$ and lengths in ratio $1: 2$. If same force is applied on them, then ratio of their change in length will be
questions.solution:
Given, ratio of radius of two wires $r_1: r_2=2: 1\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\mathrm{r}_1}{\mathrm{r}_2}=\frac{2}{1}$
and ratio in their lengths, $1_1: 1_2=1: 2\Rightarrow \quad \frac{l_1}{1_2}=\frac{1}{2}$
When same force is applied on them, then ratio r change in their length $\frac{\Delta \mathrm{l}_1}{\Delta \mathrm{l}_2}=$ ?
We know that, Young's modulus
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{Y}=\frac{\mathrm{Fl}}{\mathrm{A} \Delta \mathrm{l}} \Rightarrow \Delta \mathrm{l}=\frac{\mathrm{Fl}}{\mathrm{AY}} \\
& \Delta \mathrm{l} \propto \frac{1}{\mathrm{~A}} \\
\therefore \quad & \frac{\Delta \mathrm{I}_1}{\Delta \mathrm{I}_2}=\frac{\mathrm{l}_1}{\mathrm{~A}_1} / \frac{\mathrm{l}_2}{\mathrm{~A}_2}=\frac{\mathrm{l}_1 \mathrm{~A}_2}{\mathrm{l}_2 \mathrm{~A}_1} \\
\Rightarrow \quad & \frac{\Delta \mathrm{l}_1}{\Delta \mathrm{I}_2}=\frac{\mathrm{l}_1}{\mathrm{l}_2} \cdot \frac{\mathrm{r}_2^2}{\mathrm{r}_1^2}=\frac{1}{2} \cdot\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2=\frac{1}{8}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If ratio of terminal velocity of two drops falling in air is $3: 4$, then what is the ratio of their surface area?
questions.solution:
Terminal velocity is given by $v=\frac{2 r^2(\rho-\sigma)}{9 \eta} g$
where, $r=$ radius of drop,
$\rho=$ density of medium of drop,
$\sigma=$ density of surrounding medium
$\eta=$ coefficient of viscocity of drop medium.
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{v} \propto \mathrm{r}^2$, we know area of drop $\propto \mathrm{r}^2\Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{v} \propto \mathrm{A}$ (area) $\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{v}_1}{\mathrm{v}_2}=\frac{\mathrm{A}_1}{\mathrm{~A}_2}=\frac{3}{4}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\mathrm{A}_1}{\mathrm{~A}_2}=\frac{3}{4}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Find the height of liquid in capillary tube, if surface tension of liquid $=\mathrm{S}$, radius of capillary tube $=\mathrm{r}$ and acceleration due to gravity $=\mathrm{g}$.

questions.q: If frequency $(v)$ of light is $5 \times 10^{16} \mathrm{~Hz}$ and speed of light in air is $3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. Find the ratio of wavelength of light in a medium of refractive index ' 2 ' to air
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{v}=v \lambda$, Here, $v$ is same as source of light.
$\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{v} \propto \lambda, \frac{v_1}{v_2}=\frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_2} \\

\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Find the distance between two consecutive nodes, if for a string $\mathrm{T}=0.25 \mathrm{~N}, \mu=1 \mathrm{mg} / \mathrm{m} \mathrm{f}=250 \mathrm{~Hz}$.
questions.solution:
Given, Tension in the string, $\mathrm{T}=0.25 \mathrm{~N}$ a mass
per unit length, $\mu=1 \mathrm{mg} / \mathrm{m}=10^{-6} \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}$
Velocity of wave, $\quad v=\sqrt{\frac{T}{H}}\ldots(i)$
The distance between two consecutive nodes is equal to half the wave length ' $\lambda$ '.
$\therefore \quad v=f \lambda\ldots(ii)$
Form Eqs. (i) and (ii),
$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{f} \lambda=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{T}}{\mathrm{m}}} \Rightarrow \lambda & =\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}} \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{T}}{\mu}}=\frac{1}{250} \sqrt{\frac{0.25}{10^{-6}}} \\
\lambda & =2
\end{aligned}\therefore$ Difference between two consecutive nodes
$=\frac{\lambda}{2}=\frac{2}{2}=1 \mathrm{~m}$

questions.q: If same charge $q$ is placed inside a sphere and cube having radius 1 m and side 2 m respectively. What will be the ratio of flux passing through them?
questions.solution:
According to Gauss's law, electric flux passing through a closed surface is equal to $\frac{1}{\varepsilon_0}$ times the charge (q) enclosed by the surface
i.e.
$\phi=\frac{\mathrm{q}}{\varepsilon_0}$
Since, cube and sphere, both enclose same charge, therefore flux passing through cube and sphere is same. i.e. $\phi_{\text {sphere }}=\phi_{\text {cube }}\therefore \quad \phi_{\text {sphere }}: \phi_{\text {cube }}=1: 1$

questions.q: In the given circuit, if power rating of heater is 1000 Watt at 100 Volt, find the resistance R in figure so that heater produces power of 62.5 W.
questions.solution: Power rating of heater, $\mathrm{P}=1000 \mathrm{~W}$ Voltage rating of heater, $\mathrm{V}=100 \mathrm{~V}$ $\therefore$ Resistance of heater, $\mathrm{R}_1=\frac{\mathrm{V}^2}{\mathrm{P}}=\frac{(100)^2}{1000}=10 \Omega$ According to question, power dissipated in heater, $\mathrm{P}^{\prime}=62.5 \mathrm{~W}\therefore$ Voltage $\left(\mathrm{V}^{\prime}\right.$ ) across heater can be calculated as $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{P}^{\prime}=\frac{\left(\mathrm{V}^{\prime}\right)^2}{\mathrm{R}_1} \Rightarrow\left(\mathrm{V}^{\prime}\right)^2=\mathrm{P}^{\prime} \times \mathrm{R}_1=62.5 \times 10 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{V}^{\prime}=25 \mathrm{~V} \text { (across heater) } \\ & \end{aligned}\therefore$ Voltage across $10 \Omega$ resistor, $\mathrm{V}^{\prime \prime}=100-25=75 \mathrm{~V}$ Current in $10 \Omega$ resistor $=\frac{\mathrm{V}^{\prime \prime}}{10}=\frac{75}{10}=7.5 \mathrm{~A}$ Current in heater resistor $=\frac{\mathrm{V}^{\prime}}{10}=\frac{25}{10}=2.5 \mathrm{~A}$ So, current in $\mathrm{R} \Omega=7.5-25=5 \mathrm{~A}$ Now, $\mathrm{V}=\mathrm{IR} \Rightarrow \mathrm{R}=\mathrm{V} / \mathrm{I}=\frac{25}{5}=5 \Omega$

questions.solution: Chlorophyll-b structrally differs from chlorophyll-a by the presence of carbonyl (CHO) group at 3rd carbon in the prophyrin ring. chlorophyll-a possess methyl $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)$ group in this place.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Hardest substance in plant kingdom is
questions.solution: Sporopollenin is the hardest substance in plant kingdom. It is the major constituent of outer layer (exine) of pollen grains. It is the most resistant organic material that can withstand high temperature as well as strong acids and alkali. No enzyme is known which can degrade it.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Find odd one out.
questions.solution: Stamen is the odd one out among the other options. Stamen represent the male reproductive part of a flower, where as, stigma, style and ovary, are the parts of a carpel or pistil which represents the female reproductive part of flower.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Reproduction without actual fertilisation is called as
questions.solution:
enogenesis. It is a type of reproduction in which formation of an embryo from an unfertilised egg takes place.
Parthenocarpy is the process of production of fruit without fertilisation (pollination).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Choose the incorrect about gemmules.
options: They are asexual structure which are produce by binary fission
They can give rise to new organisms
questions.solution: Statement (c) is incorrect because Gemmules are asexual structures, produced by organisms (e.g. sponge) during unfavourable condition by the process of internal budding. They resemble endospore of bacteria. Rest statements are correct about gemmules.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Among the following choose the correct epimers.
questions.solution: Epimers are optical isomers that differ in the configuration of a single carbon atom. In the question, glucose and galactose sugars are example of epimers. They differ only in the configuration at $\mathrm{C}-4$.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Citrulline structure
questions.solution:
The correct structure of citrulline is given in option (a).
Citrulline is an amino acid. It is made from ornithine and carbamoyl phosphate in one of the control reactions in urea cycle.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Eutrophication is caused due to
questions.solution: umulation of minerals in water body. It is the process of natural ageing of lakes by the biological enrichment of its water. In a young lake, the water is clear, supporting little life with time due to the introduction of nutrients such as nitrogen and phosphorus, growth of microorganism which deteriorate the water quality take place depleting the dissolved $\mathrm{O}_2$ in water.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is not considered as a secondary messenger?
questions.solution:
Acetylcholine is not considered as a secondary messanger.
It is a common neurotransmitter present in the neuromuscular junctions, voluntary neural synapses, synapses of pre-ganglionic nerve fibres, synapses of post-ganglionic parasympathetic nerve fibres. Cholinergic nerve fibres release acetylcholine. It has excitatory effect on the skeletal muscles and excitatory or inhibitory effect at the other sites.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Bradykinin is a
questions.solution:
Bradykinin is a peptide hormone. It functions as a potent endothelium-dependent vasodilator and mild diuretic, which may cause lowering of blood pressure.
It also causes contraction of non-vascular smooth muscle in the bronchus and gut, increases vascular permeability. It is also involved in the mechanism of inflammation and pain.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Length of oesophagus is
questions.solution: The length of oesophagus is nearly 25 cm . Oesophagus is a hollow muscular tube found in vertebrates through which food is transfered from pharynx to stomach. It is about 25 centimetres long in adults. Peristaltic contractions of oesophageal muscle facilitate the passage of food through it.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In gluconeogenesis, which of the following cannot act as substrate?
questions.solution: In gluconeogenesis, fructose cannot act as substrate because it is a metabolic process by which formation of glucose from noncarbohydrate carbon substrates such as amino acid (glycine), fatty acid (glycerol, palmitic acid) etc. takes place.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Chordae tendineae is found in
questions.solution:
rt muscles of mammals.
Chordae tendineae are group of tough, tendinous strands found in the heart of mammals. They are also called as 'heart strings' due to their resemblence with small pieces of string. They play an important role in holding the atrioventricular valves in place while heart is pumping blood.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Band 3 protein in RBC has the function of
options: it mediates the exchange of cellular $\mathrm{HCO}_3^{-}$with $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$in plasma
it mediates the exchange of cations between cell and plasma
questions.solution: Band 3 protein is a typical polytropic memberane protein that mediates the exchange of cellular bicarbonate ions $\left(\mathrm{HCO}_3^{-}\right)$with the chloride $\left(\mathrm{Cl}^{-}\right)$ion in plasma, which has been known as the 'chloride shift.' Owing to this, RBC can discriminate the metabolically active cells from inactive cells and deliver oxygen particularly to metabolically active tissue that produce carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Hypothalamus can regulate
questions.solution: Thermoregulation is the ability of an organism to regulate its internal body temperature. It is under the control, of hypothalamus region of brain. Emotions like anger patience and pleasure are controlled by limbic system located in temporal lobe of brain.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is uricotelic?
questions.solution: All the given animals are uricotelic organisms. These organisms excrete uric acid as a nitrogenous waste product. Such organisms are mostly found in dry climatic conditions, thus need to conserve water in their bodies.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Atlas is
questions.solution: Atlas is the first cervical vertebrae of the spine. Along with axis, it forms the joint connecting the skull and spine.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Gastrulation means
options: a phase in which organogenesis takes places
a phase characterised by inner cell mass
questions.solution:
Gastrulation is a process by which blastocyst transforms into three layered (germ layers) structure called gastrula. These three germ layers are inner endoderm, middle mesoderm and outermost ectoderm. These three layers give rise to all tissues and organs of the developing foetus.
Conversion of morula into blastula is called blastulation. In this stage, inner cell mass is found inside the blastula. Organogenesis occur after gastrula stage.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Structure analogous to the placenta in mammals.
questions.solution: Chorion act as structure analogous to placenta in mammals. It completely encloses the developing embryo and extra embryonic tissues like placenta, it is also highly specialised to facilitate the transfer of nutrients, gases and waste between the embryo and mothers body. This is accomplised by chorionic villi that emerge from the chorion and invade the endometrium.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Number of chromosomes present in secondary spermatocyte is
questions.solution:
The number of chromosomes present in secondary spermatocyte is 23 . It is because the secondary spermatocytes are formed after the lst meiotic division (reductional division) of diploid primary spermatocytes, hence they have haploid set of chromosomes,
i.e. 23 in count.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one of the labelled part utilises fructose as a source of energy?
questions.solution:
The middle piece of the sperm utilises fructose as a source of energy. It is packed with numerous mitochondria which utilise fructose as a source of energy to provide motility to sperm to reach out ovum (egg cell)
Head is comprised of acrosome and nucleus. It has hyaluronidase enzyme in acrosome and genetic material in nucleus.
Tail it is comprised of tubulin proteins which provide motility to sperm cell.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Level of LH is maximum
questions.solution: The level of LH is maximum at the time of ovulation (i.e. ovulatory phase) in the menstrual cycle. It is called as LH surge. It induces rupture of Graafian follicles and thereby the release of ovum, i.e. ovulation.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Number of chromosomes present in spermatogonium is
questions.solution:
The number of chromosomes present is spermatogonium is 46 .
The undifferentiated, germ cells present on the inside wall of seminiferous tubules of testes are called spermatogonium (or sperm mother cells). Each spermatogonium is diploid and contains 46 chromosomes ( $44+\mathrm{XY}$ ).
At sexual maturity, these cells divide several times by mitosis to produce a large number of spermatogonia, some of which serve as stem cells for spermatogenic lineage while other act as precursor of sperms and differentiate into primary spermatocyte.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In DNA $20 \%$ bases are adenine. What percentage of bases are pyrimidines?
questions.solution:
According to chargaff's rule
$\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{G}=\mathrm{C}+\mathrm{T}=50 \%\therefore \quad$ If $\mathrm{A}=20 \%$ then $\mathrm{T}=20 \%\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{C}+\mathrm{T} & =50 \% \\
\mathrm{C}=50 \%-20 \% & =30 \%
\end{aligned}$
Total percentage of pyrimidine bases
$(\mathrm{T}+\mathrm{Q}) \text { are } 20+30=50 \%$

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Chromosome walking is
options: to see position of ribosomes on nuclear membrane
to check the expression of mutant genes
questions.solution: sed in genetic mapping. It is a method of positional cloning used to find, isolate and clone a particular allele in a gene library. It is DNA based method of genetic mapping in which the chromosome is analysed by extending one tip to reach the other. This involves systematically moving along the chromosome from a known location to an unknown location.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is not a stop codon?
questions.solution:
UAC is not a stop codon. It codes for tyrocine amino acid.
The last codon of a functional gene which helps in termination of the polypeptide chain, is termed as stop or termination codon. These are UAA, UAG and UGA.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: During DNA replication, supercoilling is relaxed by
questions.solution:
During DNA replication, super coiling is relaxed by DNA topoisomerase. These enzyme participate in the overwinding or underwinding of DNA. SSBPs are single strand binding proteins which stabilises the unwound parental DNA.
Primase this enzyme synthesise RNA primer on DNA template to initiate DNA synthesis.
RNA Polymerase enzyme helps in synthesis of new DNA strand during replication.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is not true?
options: Southern hybridisation - related to identification of RNA sequence
questions.solution: Option (d) is not correctly matched because Southern hybridisations technique is related to identification of DNA sequences. RNA sequences are indentified by Northern hybridisation.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: RNA binds to tRNA through
questions.solution:
tRNA binds to in RNA through anticodon loop, as it bears the based complementary to those on mRNA being translated.
The amino acid loop of tRNA is involved in binding the respective amino acid. The $\mathrm{T} \psi \mathrm{C}$ loop helps in binding the amino acid, while the D loop of tRNA is the binding site for aminoacyl synthetase.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Karyotype of Down's syndrome has how many chromosomes?
questions.solution: Karyotype of people suffering from Down's syndrome has 47 chromosomes ( $45+\mathrm{XY}$ in males, $45+\mathrm{XX}$ in females) instead of 46 . It is caused due to the presence of an extra chromosome number 21 , thus it is also known as 21 trisomy.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A normal man and a normal woman both having one of their parent albino, if get married then what is the probability of their child of being albino?
questions.solution:
Albinism is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern that means both parents contribute a mutated gene for the person to have albinism. So, there is a $25 \%$ chance that any of their children will have albinism. Then $50 \%$ of the children will carry the mutated gene, but will not have albinism.
The last possibility is to neither have albinism or carry the mutated gene, that's the other $25 \%$ chance.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Gynaecomastia is present in which syndrome?
questions.solution: Gynaecomastia is present in klinefelter's syndrome (XXY). It is swelling of the breast tissue in boys or men, caused by an imbalance of the hormones oestrogen and testosterone. It is commonly found in males affected with Klinefelter's syndroms. Klinefelter's syndrome is the most common sex chromosomal disorder in males. It also characterised by low testosterone and reduced muscle mass, facial and body hair.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one of them is odd with respect to human male?
questions.solution: Option (a) is incorrect/odd with respect to human male because the male karyotype has $44+\mathrm{XY}$ chromosomes. This means single X -chromosome is present with one Y-chromosomes. Barr body is an additional X-chromosome found in female somatic cells.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Coacervates were discovered by
questions.solution:
arin. They are large organic molecules synthesised abiotically on primitive earth.
They were the precursor of colloidal aggregates formed as a result of intermolecular attraction. Their presence was experimentally proved by Syduly Fox and Oparin.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one is the oldest in following?
questions.solution:
Bryophytes are the oldest (most primitive) plant type in terms of evolution.
These are the simplest and first among land inhabiting plants occupying an intermediate, position between algae and pteridophyta. They are non- vascular, terristrial, autotrophic, non-flowering and seedless plants.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Traditional anesthesia is obtained from
questions.solution: Traditionally, erythroxylum (cocaine) was used to obtain anesthesia. It has an anesthetic and analgesic property which can alleviate the pain of headache, rheumatism, wounds and sores, etc. It was also used for broken bones, childbirth and during performing trepanning operations on the skull.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Choose correct option for larva of housefly.
questions.solution: Larva of housefly is called maggot. Larva of certain beetles and other insects are called grub. Cypris is a larval form of class-Crustacea. Wriggler is a larval form of mosquitoes.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Choose the correct regarding antibodies.
questions.solution:
IgG antibody can cross placenta and provide natural passive immunity to the developing foetus. Other options are corrected as follows IgA is a dimer found in body secretions such as sweat, tears, saliva, mucus, colostrum, etc. It provide localised protections from pathogens.
IgE is involved in hypersensitive reactions and are present in mast cells and basophil cells.
IgM is found in pentamer form not as dimer.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Carcinogen present in cigarette smoke is
questions.solution: Benzopyrene is a polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon formed as a result of incomplete combustion of organic matter such as coal tar, tobacco, etc. It is a potential carcinogenic compound listed as Group 1 carcinogen by the IARC International Agency for Research on Cancer. It reacts and binds to DNA, resulting in mutation and eventually leads to cancer.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Typhoid is caused by
questions.solution:
Typhoid or Enteric fever is a bacteria borne disease caused by bacillus Salmonella typhii. It spreads through consumption of contaminated food and water. Main symptoms are high fever, headache, vomiting, loose stools, etc.
Pneumonia is caused by three different strains of bacterium named Streptococcus pneumoniae, Pneumococcus pneumoniae and Diplococcus pneumoniae. Filarial worm cause filarial disease which is also called elephantiasis. The scientific name of worm is Wuchereria bancroft.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Genetic variation cannot be effectively brought about by
questions.solution: ication. It is a technique used in molecular biology, by which multiple copies of gene or DNA sequence is produced by in vivo or in vitro methods. It has no role in introducing genetic variation in organism. It just leads to an increase in the frequency of gene.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which is also called molecular glue
questions.solution:
Enzyme DNA ligase is also called as molecule or glue, as it works to repair broken DNA by joining two nucleotides in a DNA strand. It is commonly used in genetic engineering to do the reverse of restriction enzyme, i.e,. to join together complementary restriction fragments.
DNA gyrase is an enzyme of class topoisomerase that relieves torque or strain in DNA during DNA replication. DNA helicase unwinds the double helix to make site of DNA synthesis. DNA polymerase catalyses formation of new DNA on template strand.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In annealing
options: primers anneal to the DNA template
Taq polymerase adds nucleotides to the annealed primer
two strands of the DNA separate
questions.solution: In annealing, primers anneal to the DNA template, to provide a site for initiation of polymerisation to enzyme Taq polymerase. Before this denaturation of DNA takes place in which two strands of DNA separate from each other at high temperature of $92-95^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. Extensions is last stage of PCR, in which Taq polymerase enzyme adds nucleotides to annealed primer and synthesise new strand.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: An interaction in which one organism is benefitted and other is unaffected
questions.solution:
Commensalism is a type of interaction where one organism is benefitted and other remain unaffected. In predation, one organism feeds on another organism.
In parasitism, one organism (parasite) gets the benefit at the expense of the host.
Mutualism is a type of positive interaction in which all individuals are benefitted by one another.
